messages.author: edd71c9f8bef1cf3
messages.subject: 95% CI around beta estimates
parts:
Hi all, I haven’t been able to find an answer to what may be a pretty straightforward process – calculating 95% confidence intervals around the beta coefficients for a selected best model to assess support for individual effects.

 

Is there a built-in or straightforward process for extracting the necessary information from colext output and generating confidence intervals for all included variables? Thanks for any feedback. 


msp

messages.author: edd71c9f8bef1cf3
messages.subject: Re: 95% CI around beta estimates
parts: Sorry, I meant to also ask if the included z and P(>|z|) was an appropriate metric for concluding support. Thanks!

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Re: 95% CI around beta estimates
parts:
Dear Shane,

yes, there is the confint function which does this: see this (for a dynocc model fit with colext):

> confint(fm, type = "det")
                        0.025      0.975
p(Int)              0.1136643  0.6951782
p(JulianDate)      -3.1276667 -2.2032800
p(I(JulianDate^2)) -1.7354442 -0.8717906

In contrast, I think one should not trust the z-tests in GLMs such as the dynocc.

Best regards  ---  Marc
